question: Which late Sourcery findings from merged PR #71 warrant a successor repair?

findings.description: Settings availability is misreported for default-branch names and unmappable GraphQL error paths.
findings.analysis: defaultBranchRef.name belongs to general settings, while branchProtectionRule belongs to classic protection. Pathless errors cannot safely identify any core section and must not be reported as fetched data.
findings.recommendation: Map default-branch name errors to general settings; retain classic protection for branchProtectionRule; mark every core GraphQL section unavailable for an unmappable partial error.
findings.rationale: Preserve accurate section-level availability rather than treating errored fields as fetched values.

findings.description: Partial pull-request GraphQL fields can skew issue metrics.
findings.analysis: A field-level author or merge-state error is not a known null value. Classifying it as other or not-ready makes the aggregate metrics incorrect.
findings.recommendation: Use partial-error paths to mark the affected pull-request metric group unavailable instead of deriving it from an errored field.
findings.rationale: Do not turn unavailable GraphQL fields into incorrect issue posture metrics.

findings.description: Core settings projection errors can prevent independent Actions listings.
findings.analysis: A projection failure occurs after GitHub has returned a response but before run() reaches independent REST calls. The current outer exception handler therefore incorrectly prevents recoverable Actions data from being collected.
findings.recommendation: Contain core projection failures as unavailable core data and continue with independent Actions listings.
findings.rationale: Maintain the stated independent-fetch partial-result contract.

findings.description: Mixed GraphQL field errors can assign misleading availability reasons.
findings.analysis: The current aggregate reason can mark unrelated sections forbidden. Permission metadata also occurs under extensions.type, which is not currently recognised.
findings.recommendation: Derive availability reasons from each section's matching errors and recognise extensions.code and extensions.type.
findings.rationale: Availability metadata must describe the affected section accurately.

findings.description: The settings command may exit zero after incomplete report output.
findings.analysis: The other report modes write output then propagate the ReportOutcome exit code. Settings omits that existing contract.
findings.recommendation: Apply the established post-output exit handling with focused command coverage.
findings.rationale: Automation must not receive a successful exit code when expected repository data is missing.

findings.description: Rulesets and their rules may be silently truncated at 100 entries.
findings.analysis: The first-page limit is real. Fully paginating nested rule connections would materially increase per-repository requests, but silently presenting a bounded result as complete is misleading.
findings.recommendation: Retain the bounded query and expose ruleset or rule truncation explicitly in the report.
findings.rationale: Keep the settings collector bounded while making incomplete inventory data visible.

findings.description: Inherited organisation rulesets may be excluded.
findings.analysis: Inherited rulesets were explicitly identified as useful applicable governance context in the settings change's design, but includeParents is not requested.
findings.recommendation: Request inherited parent rulesets and retain their source classification.
findings.rationale: The settings inventory should report applicable inherited governance rules without exposing bypass identities.

findings.description: Ruleset source output contains only a type, not an identity.
findings.analysis: A source type alone is insufficient to identify the governing origin of an inherited rule. The original design calls for safe repository or organisation identity where present.
findings.recommendation: Project a safe source identity alongside the source type, excluding actors and bypass data.
findings.rationale: Make inherited and repository ruleset provenance useful to maintainers.

findings.description: Additional security-and-analysis settings are not included.
findings.analysis: The requirement is for consequential security-and-analysis feature states affecting Dependabot or scanning. The current two flags omit several such repository-level states.
findings.recommendation: Collect a curated set of stable, repository-level Advanced Security, code-scanning, secret-scanning, and push-protection states.
findings.rationale: Complete the intended curated security inventory without expanding into every GitHub security setting.

findings.description: Squash merge title and message policy values are not included.
findings.analysis: Configured squash title and message behaviour is consequential merge policy and was already named in the original design, but was omitted from the projection.
findings.recommendation: Add squash merge title and message policy fields to the curated general-settings projection and schema.

findings.description: JSON repository order can vary with concurrent completion order.
findings.analysis: Concurrent execution can append otherwise identical repository results in different completion orders, creating noisy comparison output.
findings.recommendation: Sort repository results by owner and repository when projecting the JSON document.
findings.rationale: Provide stable machine-readable report ordering at negligible cost.

findings.description: A missing bypass count without a GraphQL error can conflict with the settings schema.
findings.analysis: The prior repair covers explicit bypass-field errors only. A missing count without an error path can still generate a null property that violates the schema and omission contract.
findings.recommendation: Omit unavailable bypass presence, record its availability, and cover the no-error-path case.
findings.rationale: Keep the ruleset report schema-valid and distinguish unavailable bypass data from a false value.

findings.description: The settings JSON report test lacks representative content assertions.
findings.analysis: The renderer/document consistency assertion and processor projection coverage already exercise the contract. Additional duplicated content assertions would be low-value test expansion.
findings.recommendation: Do not add the proposed assertions.
findings.rationale: Declined by maintainer: avoid unnecessary test duplication.

findings.description: Security feature-gating diagnostics misleadingly say that code scanning is disabled.
findings.analysis: GitHub's Advanced Security response establishes that Code Security is not enabled, not that the repository or its access has been disabled. The raw response is retained in structured metadata.
findings.recommendation: Translate recognised Code Security and secret-scanning feature-gating responses into canonical user-facing wording while retaining the existing unavailable reason and raw message metadata.
findings.rationale: Accepted by maintainer: distinguish unavailable product configuration from repository access.

findings.description: The Code Security wording recogniser misses GitHub's Code Security response variant.
findings.analysis: The recogniser matches only `advanced security must be enabled`, whereas the reported response says Code Security `must be enabled`. That variant follows the generic forbidden path.
findings.recommendation: Recognise both Advanced Security and Code Security wording variants and add focused coverage.
findings.rationale: Accepted by maintainer: recognise the observed GitHub response variant.

findings.description: Canonical feature-gating diagnostics are not emitted for repositories with no other security activity.
findings.analysis: The diagnostic is deferred, but deferred events flush only when a repository has alert or pull-request activity. A fully unavailable repository therefore exposes only raw JSON metadata and N/A output.
findings.recommendation: Emit recognised feature-gating diagnostics regardless of activity, retaining raw metadata separately.
findings.rationale: Accepted by maintainer: canonical configuration diagnostics must be observable even without alerts.

recommendations.rationale: Accepted or varied correctness and report-contract findings are routed in-place; the test-expansion suggestion is declined.
